Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Expectation2: Maintain a safe and O39ean work environment.
Situation2: At the end of the shift, it's time for the routine sweep-up of your designated work area.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was grabbing the broom for the end-of-shift cleanup. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his voice tight with panic. “I think I left my passport at home. Can you check and bring it to the airport? My flight’s in two hours.” I glanced around the site—dust and debris everywhere, the foreman’s words echoing in my head: “No one leaves until their area’s spotless. Safety first.” I knew if I left now, I’d be letting the crew down, maybe even risking a warning. But Sam was counting on me, desperate, and I was the only one he trusted. My hands shook as I weighed the broom in one and my phone in the other, torn between the loyalty of friendship and the responsibility of my job. The pressure built in my chest, each second ticking by, knowing I couldn’t be in two places at once.
